ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertex \(A\) of \(\square OABC\) is on the inverse proportion function \(y=\frac{1}{x}\), the vertex \(B\) is on the inverse proportion function \(y=\frac{5}{x}\), and the point \(C\) is on the positive half of the x-axis. What is the area of \(\square OABC\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line AF $\perp$ x-axis at point F through point A, and construct line BE $\perp$ x-axis at point E through point B. Extend BA to intersect the y-axis at point G. Thus, both quadrilaterals OFAG and OEBG are rectangles. \\
$\because$ Point A lies on the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{1}{x}$, and vertex B lies on the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{5}{x}$, \\
$\therefore$ Area of rectangle OFAG = 1, Area of rectangle OEBG = 5, \\
$\therefore$Area of $\square OABC$ = Area of rectangle ABEF = Area of rectangle OEBG - Area of rectangle OFAG = \boxed{4}.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, vertex \(A\) of \(\square OABC\) lies on the inverse proportion function \(y=\frac{1}{x}\), vertex \(B\) lies on the inverse proportion function \(y=\frac{5}{x}\), and point \(C\) is on the positive x-axis. What is the area of \(\square OABC\)?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Construct line AF \(\perp\) x-axis at point F through point A, and construct line BE \(\perp\) x-axis at point E through point B. Extend BA to intersect the y-axis at point G. Thus, both quadrilaterals OFAG and OEBG are rectangles. Because point A lies on \(y=\frac{1}{x}\), and point B lies on \(y=\frac{5}{x}\), Area\((\text{OFAG})=1\), Area\((\text{OEBG})=5\). Therefore, Area\((\square OABC)\) = Area\((\text{ABEF})\) = Area\((\text{OEBG})\) - Area\((\text{OFAG})\) = \(\boxed{4}\).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a plane rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin, and C is on the positive x-axis; quadrilateral OABC is drawn as a parallelogram, AB is a horizontal line segment and is parallel to OC, and OA and BC are oblique sides and are parallel to each other. Point A is on the inverse proportional function curve closer to the inside; the problem text gives that A is on y=1/x. Point B is on another inverse proportional function curve; the problem text gives that B is on y=5/x. Reasoning: Draw perpendiculars from A and B respectively to the x-axis, with feet F and E; extend the horizontal line BA to the left to intersect the y-axis at G. Since AB is horizontal, OFAG and OEBG are both rectangles. For a point (x,y) on the inverse proportional function y=k/x in the first quadrant, the area of the rectangle with the origin and that point as opposite vertices is xy=k. Therefore, the area of rectangle OFAG is 1, and the area of rectangle OEBG is 5. The difference between the two rectangles is exactly rectangle ABEF, with area 5-1=4. Also because parallelogram OABC and rectangle ABEF have the same horizontal base AB and the same height, their areas are equal. Therefore, the area of □OABC is 4.
